blocks.text: Steelcast is a single-site steel foundry in Bhavnagar, Gujarat, that pours carbon, low-alloy, high-alloy and manganese steel castings of 5 kg to 2,500 kg and sells them, mostly machined, to heavy-equipment OEMs [F] (AR2026 p.30) [F] (SCREENER). It makes money by converting scrap and ferro-alloys into engineered components priced under a sales-price-variation formula that resets for input costs with about a one-quarter lag [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). About 75% of castings ship fully machined [MC] (AR2026 p.8). It reports one segment, castings [F] (AR2026 p.68).

subsections.title: Listing status and what it means for the evidence base

blocks.text: This is not a recent listing. The business began as a partnership in 1960, became a private company in 1972 and a public company in 1994 [F] (RATING). It trades on BSE (513517) and NSE (STEELCAS) [F] (AR2026 p.117). No prospectus applies and none was available. The evidence base is ten years of audited standalone statements [F] (AR2026 p.54), four earnings calls, one presentation and a CARE rating note. No subsidiaries exist, so standalone equals group [F] (AR2026 p.68).

The weakness in the evidence is disclosure quality, not history. Customers are anonymised, segment margins are not reported, and management's own numbers for GET share, capacity, headcount, scrap sourcing and export geography conflict across documents. We show each conflict rather than choosing between them [AI].

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. The price discounts a growth path no document supports: the reverse DCF needs ~63% annual sales growth for five years, against 7.1% in our base case [E] (NUMBERS). Management's own aspiration is ~20% CAGR [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
2. Customer concentration is worsening at the top: the largest group rose from 32.4% of revenue in FY25 to 37.6% in FY26, and the top three account for 78.3% [E] from [F] (AR2026 p.209).
3. The revenue base is cyclical: mining plus earthmoving was 76% of total operating income in FY26 [F] (RATING), and sales fell 22% from FY23 to FY25 [F] (NUMBERS).

4. Profit growth was flattered: excluding the Rs 8.46 cr forex gain in FY26, and the Rs 2.78 cr forex gain and Rs 2.32 cr LB Steel write-off in FY25, pre-tax profit grew ~11.5% rather than the reported 19.7% [E] from [F] (AR2026 p.200-202).

5. Guidance is unstable and was missed last year: FY26 growth guidance was cut from 18-20% to ~12% [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). The FY27 figure has moved between 20%+, 25% and 30% within two months [MC] (CALL Jun 2026, CALL Aug 2026).
6. Q1 FY27 volume grew only 11.6% YoY (3,618 t to 4,036 t) against a 25% volume guide [E] from [F] (PPT Aug 2026). Rs 14.4 cr of WIP and finished goods was built in the quarter [F] (PPT Aug 2026).
7. The diversification story is thin in the numbers: GET was Rs 1.37 cr (0.3%) of FY26 sales [F] (AR2026 p.132). Defence has been deprioritised and the US railroad effort paused [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
8. Capex discipline moved: the stated trigger was 75% utilisation [MC] (AR2026 p.23) (CALL Feb 2026), yet a Rs 120 cr greenfield was approved at ~63% [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

9. Governance signals are mixed: the CMD pledged or encumbered 1.48% of total shares during FY26, from nil at the start of the year [F] (AR2026 p.98). The statutory auditor changed at the July 2025 AGM [F] (AR2026 p.70). Promoter-family executive pay was Rs 7.54 cr, about 8.7% of FY26 PAT [E] from [F] (AR2026 p.101).

10. Disclosure inconsistencies reduce the reliability of management's operating claims: capacity is given as 29,000 or 30,000 TPA, headcount as 1,081, ~700, 1,655 or 'over 1,600', and GET share as 0.3% or 1.1% [F] (AR2026 p.14, p.18, p.25, p.27, p.30, p.47, p.132) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

Are margins structural? Bull: OPM rose from 20% (FY21) to 29% (FY24) and held at 27-28% through a volume downcycle [F] (NUMBERS). Bear: management itself calls 25-26% EBITDA the sustainable level [MC] (CALL Jun 2026, CALL Nov 2025), and FY26 headline margins included forex gains [F] (AR2026 p.200). The market may be capitalising management's 28-30% including-other-income figure rather than 25-27% [AI].

Is the greenfield a demand signal or a capacity bet? Management says customers are asking for more [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Yet the order book covers only ~3-4 months [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), no LTAs are disclosed, and FY29 volume needs ~88% growth over FY26 to hit 90% of existing capacity [E]. It could prove prescient if the new-part pipeline converts [AI].

Concentration: CARE argues it is mitigated because more than 17 legal entities sit inside the three groups, each with separate approvals [F] (RATING). The counter-view is that group-level purchasing decisions, not entity-level approvals, drive volumes, and the top group's share is rising [AI].

Is the re-rating earned? At 31 Mar 2026 the stock traded at Rs 225.8 on a P/E of 26.3x [F] (AR2026 p.118). It now trades at Rs 371 and 41.2x TTM [F] (NUMBERS), while TTM EPS rose only from 8.58 to 8.95 [F] (NUMBERS). The market has re-rated guidance rather than delivered earnings [AI].

Is Steelcast underestimated? A debt-free foundry at 48% utilisation with a price-variation formula and multi-year OEM approvals could compound faster than a trailing-growth DCF allows. Our base DCF starts at 4.3% growth against a 25% guide [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

blocks.text: **Variant perception** [AI]: The consensus framing, visible in our own earlier board notes, is a quality foundry with pricing power and a de-risking story. We agree about the quality of the balance sheet and the pass-through mechanism. We disagree on two points. First, the de-risking is overstated: sector diversification exists mainly in presentations (GET 0.3%, defence ~1%), while customer-group concentration at the top rose in FY26. Second, the price already assumes flawless delivery of an aspiration (20-30% growth), whereas the documents evidence only a ~3-4 month order book and a Q1 volume run-rate of +11.6%. Even the most generous point in our DCF sensitivity grid (Rs 97.6) is about 74% below the price [E] (NUMBERS). The investable debate is therefore not whether Steelcast is a good business, but how much of FY29 is already in the price.

blocks.text: The company holds Rs 3.44 cr of equity and Rs 3.97 cr of CCDs in the two AMP entities [F] (AR2026 p.187). We read these as the equity stakes the group-captive power model requires, not as strategic investments [AI].

The foundry is old (66 years), but the current earnings profile is recent [AI]. Before FY22, revenue never exceeded Rs 318 cr and OPM sat at 19-20% [F] (NUMBERS). The step-up to 24-29% OPM and Rs 70-90 cr PAT dates only from FY23, coinciding with captive renewable power (2023) and a volume peak [F] (NUMBERS) (AR2026 p.73). So the 'high-margin through the cycle' record rests on three to four years, one of which (FY25) was a downturn year [AI]. The management team below the promoter family joined the Board only in 2023, and the auditor changed in 2025 [F] (AR2026 p.63, p.70).

items: 1. Development: the OEM issues a development order with a tooling and sample PO. Development takes 6-7 months, down from 12 [MC] (AR2026 p.24), or from ~9 months to 6 [MC] (AR2026 p.42) [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).
2. Pattern, tooling and simulation: in-house simulation-led validation and a DST-recognised R&D lab [F] (AR2026 p.36).

3. Inputs: steel scrap and ferro-alloys [F] (RATING). Scrap comes from automobile and engineering sources, with Alang-linked scrap capped at 20-25% [MC] (AR2026 p.33). Management contradicted this on the Q1 call: 'Steelcast does not use any raw material from the ship breaking' [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
4. Melting: induction furnaces [F] (AR2026 p.73).
5. Moulding and core-making: no-bake, automated fast-loop no-bake and shell moulding [F] (RATING); cold-box cores and vertical centrifugal casting [MC] (AR2026 p.36-37).
6. Pouring, cooling and fettling: automated pouring and cooling lines, with mechanised fettling [MC] (AR2026 p.36, p.42).
7. Heat treatment: including a 20 t double-door furnace and polymer quenching [MC] (AR2026 p.36).
8. Testing: NABL-accredited lab, radiography and CMM/FARO metrology [F] (AR2026 p.30, p.36).
9. Machining: ~75% of castings shipped fully machined, including five-axis CNC [MC] (AR2026 p.8, p.36).
10. Logistics: Pipavav port (130 km) and the Ghogha-Hazira Ro-Pax ferry [MC] (AR2026 p.33).
11. Billing: the price-variation formula passes raw-material and fuel moves through with about a one-quarter lag, and rupee moves are shared with the customer [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).

subsections.title: Where value is captured and why

blocks.text: Value is captured in conversion, not materials. In FY26, cost of materials consumed was only Rs 84.9 cr (20% of revenue) [F] (AR2026 p.200). Stores and spares (Rs 56.6 cr), power and fuel (Rs 44.0 cr) and other manufacturing expenses (Rs 48.6 cr) together exceeded materials [F] (AR2026 p.201). Management's 'Total Raw Material and Value Add' line was 56.3% of FY26 revenue [E] from [F] (PPT Aug 2026). Margin comes from yield, energy cost (captive renewables) and machining content, and is protected by the formula-based pass-through [AI]. The weak point is that the OEM holds the specification and can re-source over 2-3 years [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

Outsourcing is not disclosed as a separate line. 'Other manufacturing expenses' of Rs 48.6 cr may include job work, but the AR does not break it out [F] (AR2026 p.201) [AI]. Capital intensity is moderate. Net fixed assets are Rs 158 cr against revenue of Rs 423 cr, a fixed-asset turnover of 2.68x [F] (NUMBERS). The new foundry costs ~Rs 1.41 lakh per tonne of capacity (Rs 120 cr / 8,500 t) [E] from [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). We classify the model as moderately capital-heavy but self-funding at current margins [AI].

Differentiated [AI]: high-integrity, heat-treated, machined castings for mining and earthmoving OEMs that require multi-stage approvals, and approval-heavy niches (AAR rail, EN 9100 aerospace, defence). The differentiated niches are the smallest revenue lines today. Realisation per tonne rose only 2.4% in FY26 (Rs 2.97 to Rs 3.04 lakh/t) [E] from [F] (AR2026 p.39, p.172), which does not yet show a mix shift toward premium products [AI].

subsections.title: Segment margins and why segments moved

blocks.text: Segment margins are not disclosed. The company reports a single Ind AS 108 segment [F] (AR2026 p.208).

items: Mining: export sales rose from Rs 70.0 cr to Rs 101.1 cr on 'improvement in international mining equipment demand' [MC] (AR2026 p.131). [AI] This is the single biggest FY26 driver and is cyclical.
Earthmoving: exports rose from Rs 101.8 cr to Rs 129.9 cr as 'global equipment inventories normalise' [MC] (AR2026 p.131). [AI] This reads as restocking, not share gain.

Construction: domestic sales fell from Rs 72.1 cr to Rs 68.6 cr, with 'strong indications' seen late in the year [MC] (AR2026 p.131). [AI] The expected domestic recovery has not yet shown in the numbers.
Rail/loco: fell despite AAR certification [F] (AR2026 p.131); the US railroad effort was paused [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). [AI] Optionality has been downgraded.
GET: fell from Rs 1.67 cr to Rs 1.37 cr [F] (AR2026 p.132), while management guides a 10-20x rise in share by FY29 [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). [AI] Unproven.

blocks.text: All segments are schedule-driven OEM supply against rolling ~3-4 month firm orders, not project or tender orders [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). Defence is the only line that is prototype- and approval-gated [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). New-part development orders from existing customers are the organic lever [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Growth therefore depends on OEM build rates and new-part wins, not on a backlog [AI].

blocks.text: The export geography data do not reconcile [AI]. The AR puts the Americas at 34.5% of exports [F] (AR2026 p.13). Management says the US alone was 26-27% of total sales, which would be ~43-45% of exports [MC] (CALL Feb 2026) [E]. subsections.title: Export mix: strategy or mix? Currency exposure

blocks.text: FY26's rise in export share (53% to 60%) came from mining and earthmoving export recovery, not from new geographies. The country count moved only from 15-16 to 16 [MC] (CALL Nov 2025) (AR2026 p.13) [AI]. Management itself describes the export share as fluctuating within a 45-65% band [MC] (CALL Nov 2025, CALL Feb 2026). It guides FY27 exports at 49-50% of volume and FY28 at 47% [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). That conflicts with the 62% Q1 value share and with a February guide of 60% for FY27 [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

Currency: management says rupee depreciation and appreciation are shared with customers [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The AR says a hedging policy exists and hedges are used 'whenever required' [MC] (AR2026 p.115, p.120). CARE says there is no active hedging policy [F] (RATING). FY26 forex gain was Rs 8.46 cr, 7.3% of PBT [F] (AR2026 p.200) [E]. Foreign-exchange outgo was only Rs 6.39 cr against earnings of Rs 250.1 cr [F] (AR2026 p.74), so the natural hedge is negligible [AI].

subsections.title: Tariffs, trade policy and single-location risk

items: US tariffs: the additional US tariff burden on Indian goods is 50% [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Disruption began 'starting April' [MC] (CALL Nov 2025; the transcript says April '26, which appears to mean April 2025 [AI]). Three customers asked for cost-sharing, and no price cut was given [MC] (CALL Nov 2025).
FY26 guidance was cut from 18-20% to ~12% because of tariffs [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). Actual growth was 13.3% [F] (AR2026 p.67).

EU: duties are ~6-6.5% today, and the impact of the India-EU FTA is unknown [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). A UK agreement lowered tariffs on steel castings [MC] (CALL Nov 2025). EU CBAM is flagged as a sector risk [F] (AR2026 p.130).

Single location: all capacity is in Bhavnagar [F] (RATING). The greenfield is 12 km from the existing plant [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), so regional concentration (power, gas, port, labour, cyclone) persists after expansion [AI].

No long-term agreements, volume commitments or take-or-pay terms are disclosed. The relationship runs on price-variation formulas, a ~3-month firm schedule rolled monthly, and tooling/sample POs [MC] (CALL Aug 2026, CALL Feb 2026). Trade receivable terms are 30-145 days, and only 0.9% of receivables were more than six months past due [F] (AR2026 p.189-190) [E].

Both readings hold, depending on the measure [AI]. Top-three share improved slightly (80.1% to 78.3%) and sits at the low end of CARE's historical 75-88% range [E] (RATING). Top-one share worsened (32.4% to 37.6%) [E]. Sector concentration also worsened, with mining plus earthmoving rising from ~72% to ~77% of sector revenue [E] from [F] (AR2026 p.131). The claims of 30-35 new customers [F] (RATING) and ~50 OEM customers [MC] (AR2026 p.25) have not reduced group-level dependence. On the balance of evidence, concentration is worsening at the top [AI].

subsections.title: Why TAM cannot be translated into company revenue

blocks.text: The India market figure is dominated by automotive, cast and ductile iron, and die-casting, none of which Steelcast makes. Its niche is heavy steel and alloy-steel castings for mining, earthmoving and construction OEMs, a segment no document sizes [F] (AR2026 p.129) [AI]. Illustrative arithmetic only: at an assumed Rs 85/USD (our assumption, not from the documents), FY26 revenue of Rs 423 cr is ~USD 50 m [E]. That is ~0.19% of the India foundry market and ~0.03% of the global market [E]. These ratios say nothing about achievable share, because most of the TAM is not addressable [AI].

items: Capacity ceiling: 29,000 TPA existing plus 8,500 TPA greenfield [F] (AR2026 p.30) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026).
Realisation: ~Rs 3.04 lakh/t in FY26 [E] (AR2026 p.39, p.172).
Demand: the wallet of three OEM groups (Rs 331 cr of FY26 purchases from Steelcast [E] (AR2026 p.209)) plus new-part wins. This depends on OEM build rates, not on the TAM [AI].

On this framing, the revenue opportunity to FY29 is bounded at roughly Rs 0.8-1.0k cr at FY26 prices if everything fills [E] (sensitivity in the operations part). Management's Rs 860 cr to Rs 1,000 cr FY29 aspirations sit at the top of that range [MC] (CALL Jun 2026, CALL Nov 2025).

blocks.text: Supply is fragmented (4,500-5,000 Indian foundries) [F] (AR2026 p.129), while demand is concentrated in a handful of global mining and earthmoving OEMs [AI]. The channel is direct: 100% of sales go to OEMs and more than 98% are Tier-1, with no distributors or replacement market [MC] (CALL Nov 2025, CALL Aug 2026). Bargaining power therefore sits with the buyer, and the price-variation formula is the supplier's main protection [AI].

But a meaningful slice of recent growth came from treasury income and currency, and the underlying pre-tax growth rate is roughly half the headline [E]. Our forecast is the base case of our DCF model, unchanged [F] (NUMBERS). The model starts from TTM revenue of Rs 441 cr (June 2026) and fades growth linearly from a starting rate to a year-5 rate. EBITDA is at a fixed margin. FCFF is EBITDA less tax on EBIT, less capex (depreciation plus new sales divided by fixed-asset turnover), less the change in working capital. A Gordon terminal value closes the model, and equity equals EV less borrowings [F] (NUMBERS). Because the model rolls from a June-2026 TTM base, Year 1 roughly corresponds to FY27, and fiscal labels are approximate [AI].

blocks.text: Compounding 63.2% for five years multiplies revenue ~11.6x [E]. Running both the existing 29,000 TPA and the planned 8,500 TPA at full capacity at FY26 realisation would lift revenue only ~2.7x [E]. The implied growth is therefore physically impossible with announced capacity, and would require several further greenfields, higher realisation, or both [AI].

The price requires growth roughly nine times the base case, five times the bull case's year-5 rate, and about three times management's own aspiration [E] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026). The rule-based flag in our model reads 'Price needs growth well above trend' [F] (NUMBERS). Nothing in the documents (order book of ~3-4 months, Q1 volume +11.6%, top-group concentration of 37.6%) evidences that trajectory [AI].

A five-year DCF with a 5.5% terminal growth and a 15% discount rate structurally undervalues a business that could compound at ~20% for a decade. The market may be paying for duration: 48% utilisation today, a self-funded greenfield, a 144-part pipeline, China+1 export demand and a clean balance sheet [F] (NUMBERS) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026, CALL Feb 2026) [AI]. Small, under-owned exporters (2.8% institutional ownership) can re-rate on scarcity [F] (NUMBERS) [AI]. For balance, we note this argument, but it explains a premium to the DCF, not a 4-7x premium [AI].

summary.one_line: Steelcast is a debt-free, cash-generative steel foundry with real operating leverage, but its revenue is concentrated in three OEM groups and cyclical end-markets. At Rs 371 the price sits 4-7x above every DCF scenario and implies ~63% annual growth that no disclosed order book, capacity plan or management aspiration supports.
